meta.title: CS50 AP -- extended (weeks 0-6 remainder)

locator_titles.0: Week 0: Scratch -- everything but data representation (computational thinking, abstraction, algorithms, pseudocode, Scratch constructs)
locator_titles.4: Week 4: Memory -- everything but data representation (pointers, segmentation faults, dynamic memory allocation, stack, heap, buffer overflow)

meta.caveat: Mapped from CS50 AP's own published per-week topic lists (https://cs50.harvard.edu/ap/2025/curriculum/x/weeks/<n>/), not from an audit of lecture or problem-set content -- comparable confidence to codehs_corgi, not cmu_cs1. The weeks-0-and-4 split between 'data representation' and everything else in those weeks is this teacher's own editorial cut, not a division CS50 itself draws; see cs50ap for the other half.

1.4.note: Debugging ('Step through', 'Step into'), a named week-2 topic with its own Shorts, is finding and fixing a mistake in a program.

3.1.note: Variables is a named topic in both C (week 1) and Python (week 6).

3.2.note: Strings and Arrays (week 2) and Abstract Data Types (week 5) are all ways of building a data abstraction on top of a single variable.

3.3.note: Operators is a named week-1 topic; Integer Overflow and Floating-Point Imprecision are what happens when a mathematical expression's result doesn't fit its type.

3.4.note: Strings is a named week-2 topic.

3.5.note: Python's own topic line names 'Boolean Expressions' directly.

3.6.note: Conditionals (C) and Conditionals (Python) are both named topics.

3.8.note: Loops is a named topic in both weeks.

3.10.note: Arrays (week 2) and the list-like Abstract Data Types -- Queues, Stacks, Linked Lists (week 5) -- are both named.

3.12.note: Functions is a named Shorts topic in week 2 and an explicit topic ('Functions, Arguments, Return Values') in week 6.

3.13.note: Same functions claim as 3.12 -- writing them, not just calling them.

3.14.note: Header Files, Libraries, and Manual Pages (week 1) and Modules, Packages (week 6) are both named topics.

9-12.CS.2.note: Source Code -> Compiler -> Machine Code (week 1) and pointers/stack/heap (week 4) are the software-and-hardware layers this standard names, made visible instead of hidden.

9-12.CS.3.note: Debugging, plus reliance on Manual Pages, is troubleshooting a problem through research and testing.

9-12.AP.13.note: Arrays (week 2) and the named Abstract Data Types (week 5) are collections replacing separately named variables.

9-12.AP.14.note: The same Conditionals/Loops task reads and runs differently in C versus Python -- a real, named-topic-grounded control-structure choice.

9-12.AP.16.note: Functions (named in both weeks) are decomposition into a subproblem solved on its own.

9-12.AP.17.note: Libraries (week 1) and Modules/Packages (week 6) are modular design built from code someone else wrote.

9-12.NI.7.note: Cryptography, a named week-2 topic (Caesar and Vigenère ciphers in the problem set), is a symmetric-key technique for protecting data.

HS-ALG-PS-01.note: Choosing the right data structure -- queue, stack, linked list, tree, hash table -- for a job is the whole week.

HS-PRO-PD-12.note: Functions, named in both weeks, are splitting a program into well-organized pieces.

HS-PRO-PD-13.note: Manual Pages, a named week-1 topic, are exactly the reference documentation this standard describes leaning on.

HS-PRO-VD-16.note: Arrays (week 2) and the named data structures (week 5) are choosing the right structure to hold a program's data.

5.9.note: Functions, named in both weeks, are breaking a large problem into smaller components.

5.10.note: Abstraction is a named week-0 topic; the Source Code/Compiler/Machine Code pipeline (week 1) and Abstract Data Types (week 5) are both layers that let you work with a system without tracking every detail underneath.

5.8.note: Algorithms and Pseudocode, named week-0 topics, introduce algorithms as a general problem-solving tool before any specific language.

10.8.note: Cryptography, a named week-2 topic, is this standard's own 'encryption' concept.

C4.1.note: C (week 1) and Python (week 6) are named, back-to-back, as this teacher's own low-level-to-high-level range.

C4.4.note: Types is a named week-1 topic; Integer Overflow and Floating-Point Imprecision are what it means for a type to have a specific encoding with real limits.

C4.6.note: Syntax Highlighting, a named week-1 topic (in VS Code), foregrounds that C has its own syntax to use correctly.

C4.7.note: Arrays (week 2) and the named data structures (week 5) are this standard's own list of ways to organize a program's data.

C4.9.note: Conditionals, Loops, and Functions -- named in both weeks -- are the shared toolkit this standard describes.

C5.4.note: Debugging, a named week-2 topic with two dedicated Shorts, is testing applied as its own distinct step.

C5.6.note: Same claim as C5.4 -- debugging named directly, not folded into 'writing code.'
